text:
She has already kissed Antony's dead lips,

has wept on her knees before Caesar

and her servants have betrayed her. Darkness falls.

The trumpets of the Roman eagle shriek.


Here comes the last man seized by her beauty,

—such a gallant suitor—with a shamefaced murmur:

"You will have to walk before him, like a slave, in the triumph."

But the slope of her swan neck is calmer

than ever.


Tomorrow they will chain her children. Nothing remains for her

but to drive that fellow mad

and place the black asp, as a merciful separation,

upon her dark breast, with indifferent hand.




1940

translation.title: Cleopatra
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Cleopatra's poise between humiliation, threat, and the merciful asp.
